analysis: The PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md. The visible changes are the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and the performance_measurements section (head lines 578-584): sample_age_ms is now the elapsed time since the newest observation, applied independently per workload bucket and current-posture series in EnginePerformanceMeasurements.swift. Completed samples keep receipt-order EWMA and sample counts, and no wire fields change. This is documentation of a Swift producer behavior, and I could not review the producer source because it was not supplied. The data is observational telemetry that the doc says does not gate routing or admission (lines 424-426 and the clamp and freshness notes for the other telemetry blocks). It does not touch the TB-002 or TB-011 authorization, attestation, encryption or final-handoff paths. The threat model treats provider-reported fields as untrusted, and the provider can already misreport this data. An age rule that depends on newest-observation time is a metric-integrity detail, not a trust boundary change. The coordinator's clamping and freshness handling of performance_measurements is outside the supplied evidence. Remaining question: whether the coordinator treats performance_measurements as untrusted or bounded input in practice. The doc states these are transient routing observations, so a malicious provider could skew its own scheduling signals, which is pre-existing and not introduced here. No regression identified.
